subject: Private GPU pool: jitter mitigation, sizing matrix and network constraints
messages:
From: Brian Lowe <brian@atlashealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Atlas Health - Platform Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private GPU pool sizing — target throughput, jitter, and network constraints

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. We’re kicking off a private deployment (VPC peering from our AWS account) to run a 13B generative model for patient-centric summarization. High level asks:
- Steady-state throughput target: 1,800–2,200 qps (inference requests) for short prompts (avg 60 tokens output).
- Latency objective: p90 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms if possible.
- Tight tail/jitter control — we will have a hard SLA to our internal teams for p99.5.
- Network constraints: limited egress (100 Mbps per node) and a cross-account VPC peering link with 10 Gbps aggregate.

Can you recommend an initial private GPU pool sizing plan, autoscale policy (target headroom), and any networking mitigations (MTU, NIC settings, MTU, jumbo frames, keepalives) we should be aware of? Also note we will need an operational canary plan and fallback to a smaller model variant on overload.

Happy to hop on a quick 30m if that helps.

—Brian
Brian Lowe
Director, Platform Engineering
Atlas Health
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing — target throughput, jitter, and network constraints

Brian — thanks, this is great detail. I sketched an initial sizing matrix and attached a working spreadsheet (sizing-matrix-v1.xlsx) with assumptions: model: 13B dense, 60 token avg response, batching latency budget 30ms per token, KV cache hit expected for ~35% of requests.

High-level proposal (starter):
- Baseline nodes: 8 x A100-80GB (single-socket) with 4 workers per GPU (tuned to your prompt lengths). Estimated sustainable qps: ~220–260 qps per GPU with continuous batching and prefix cache warm; ~1,800–2,080 qps headroom across the pool.
- Autoscale policy: target 30% free capacity headroom (scale up when avg utilization > 70% over 90s window). Burst nodes (spot/dedicated spare) for 20% temporary capacity.
- Tail/jitter controls: dedicated low-latency pathway (priority queue) for p90 traffic, token-level preemption for long-running requests, and strict max-batch-size to bound intra-batch latency.
- Network: enable jumbo MTU 9001 on the GPU subnet, Bonded NICs with LACP for resiliency, and flow-control settings to avoid drops; limit inter-node egress per node at the hypervisor (100 Mbps cap) to protect our peering link.

Attachments: sizing-matrix-v1.xlsx (contains per-GPU qps estimates, warmup impact, and cost tradeoffs).

Next steps: Marissa / Naomi / Sean — can you comment on these assumptions and add operational runbooks? Brian — if the numbers look directionally right, happy to schedule a 30m to go over the canary plan and fallback model variant.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing — target throughput, jitter, and network constraints

Looping in a few concrete recommendations from product/ops perspective:

1) Sizing math (conservative): assume 200 qps sustained per GPU for 13B with quantization + continuous batching. Given failure / cache-warm variance, start with 10 GPUs (2 extra for headroom) — target pool 10 GPUs across 3 availability zones for fault isolation.

2) Autoscale policy:
- Scale up: when 5-min moving avg > 68% GPU util OR queue length > 30 requests for > 45s.
- Scale down: maintain a 10-minute cooloff and only scale down when util < 45% for 3 consecutive 60s windows.

3) Canary + fallback:
- Canary: warm a 2 GPU canary in staging with identical traffic replay (10% traffic) for 24h. Watch p50/p90/p99 latency and token failure rate.
- Fallback model: maintained 6B variant (quantized) that we can route to automatically at node or route-level when p99 exceeds 600ms for > 5m. Circuit breaker to reject low-priority requests rather than impacting all traffic.

4) Observability & SLOs:
- Instrument per-request kv-cache-hit flags and batch sizes. Alert when p90 latency increases > 20% over baseline within 10m.

I added the sizing spreadsheet notes to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSizing — please review.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing — target throughput, jitter, and network constraints

Operational notes from infra/ops POV — quick checklist and risks: 

- Network: confirm cross-account peering supports MTU 9001 (some transit gateways strip jumbo frames). If not, fall back to TCP tuning (tune rmem/wmem, enable GSO/GRO) and use keepalives (30s).
- Egress shaping: implement token-bucket policing at the node egress to honor the 100 Mbps per-node constraint. Test with synthetic bursts to validate backpressure into the request queue.
- Time sync: strict NTP/PTP across nodes to avoid cache stampede at warmup.
- OS/hypervisor: ensure NIC drivers are latest and interrupt moderation tuned for small packet sizes.
- Canary plan: run a 24h production-like replay with gradual ramp (0 -> 10% in 30m) and exercise fallback route to 6B model at least once to validate correctness.
- Failure modes: plan for graceful degradation — drop low-priority batched requests, route short prompts to a lighter model, and pause non-critical background jobs.

I will prepare an ops runbook (network-checklist.pdf) and a short playbook for incident responders outlining steps 1–7. Attaching checklist in next email.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference
